# Results — Study 958 (Spot ETF Basis) on the real daily tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The question: after the
January-2024 US spot bitcoin ETFs, is the futures-vs-spot carry still there, and did it
**compress** at the launch? We measure each wrapper's **tracking difference** against a
bitcoin reference — the cumulative log gap `log(W/W0) - log(S/S0)` — and read its
annualised drag as the HAC-robust **OLS slope on calendar time** — then repeat every
headline on a deliberately blunt **non-overlapping monthly** estimator that needs no HAC
assumption, because a trend *t* on a persistent level flatters. Daily total-return
closes (`yfinance`, `auto_adjust=True`; BITO's very large distributions are reinvested —
price-only would manufacture most of the "drag"). As-of **2026-06-30** (the partial
current month is dropped).*

## Data stamp

| Legs | Window | n days | Fingerprint |
|---|---|---|---|
| BITO (futures wrapper), BTC-USD (coin) | 2021-10-20 → 2026-06-30 | 1,177 | Fingerprint `b7f384a06a79` |
| IBIT, FBTC (spot wrappers), BIL (cash) | 2024-01-11 → 2026-06-30 | 618 | same frame |

**Assumptions, not measurements** (labelled everywhere they are used, and swept):
expense ratios BITO 0.95%, IBIT 0.25%, FBTC 0.25% (prospectus headline; IBIT waived to
0.12% on the first $5bn for 12 months, FBTC to 0.00% until 2024-07-31); the collateral
yield proxied by BIL's total return; the short-borrow rate on the harvest leg; 5 bps
one-way cost × NAV. The event date 2024-01-11 is the first spot-ETF session.

## Why the estimator is a trend slope, not a mean of daily differences

`BTC-USD` is a 24/7 quote stamped at 00:00 UTC; the ETFs mark at 16:00 New York. Because
daily log differences telescope, `252 × mean(daily diff)` is *exactly* the two-endpoint
estimator, and each endpoint carries a fat intraday offset. The trend slope uses all
*n* observations instead, so that offset averages down. The two spot wrappers calibrate
the ruler against a **known** cost — their own fee:

| Wrapper | Trend slope | HAC *t* | Naive (endpoint) estimator | Published fee |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **IBIT** | **−0.250%/yr** (se 0.049) | −5.09 | −0.416%/yr (*t* = −0.07) | −0.25%/yr |
| **FBTC** | **−0.205%/yr** (se 0.047) | −4.33 | −0.459%/yr (*t* = −0.08) | −0.25%/yr (waived to 2024-07-31) |

The trend slope reads IBIT's 25 bp fee **to the basis point**, and reads FBTC a shade
cheaper — precisely as its six-month launch waiver implies. The endpoint estimator, on
the same data, cannot distinguish either from zero. That is the ruler this study uses.

## The carry is emphatically still there

Three estimators of the same quantity, from the most efficient to the most conservative.
The third — the mean of **non-overlapping month-end gaps**, with an ordinary *t* — is the
one the verdict leans on, because it needs no HAC assumption at all.

| Pair | Window | n | Trend drag | HAC *t* | Naive (endpoint) drag (*t*) | Monthly non-overlapping drag (plain *t*) |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| BITO vs BTC-USD | full | 1,177 | **−5.69%/yr** (se 0.16) | −35.8 | −5.53% (−1.36) | −5.28% (−2.09, 56 m) |
| BITO vs BTC-USD | post-launch | 618 | **−5.97%/yr** (se 0.20) | −29.3 | −5.65% (−1.02) | −5.63% (−2.17, 29 m) |
| BITO vs IBIT | post-launch | 618 | −5.72%/yr (se 0.19) | −30.7 | −5.23% (**−7.24**) | −5.48% (**−9.83**, 29 m) |
| BITO vs FBTC | post-launch | 618 | −5.77%/yr (se 0.20) | −29.6 | −5.19% (−7.03) | −5.50% (−8.92, 29 m) |

**Read the *t*'s in that order, not the other way round.** The trend slope regresses a
serially dependent level on time; its HAC *t* is the most generous number in the table
and should be treated as an upper bound on the evidence, not as the evidence. The residual
diagnostics say exactly how much to discount it: against the coin the residual is
comfortably stationary (AR(1) 0.740, Dickey-Fuller *t* = **−7.46**) so the trend *t* means
something there, but against IBIT and FBTC it is pinned near a unit root (AR(1) 0.981 and
0.982, DF *t* = **−3.00** and **−2.51** — short of the ≈ −3.4 needed to reject), so on the
matched-close pairs the *t* = −30 is not to be believed and the monthly column is. Against the
*coin* the assumption-light estimators are much weaker — |*t*| ≈ 2.1, because sixteen
hours of bitcoin sits in every endpoint — so the certification rests on the two
**matched-close** pairs, where every estimator agrees: −5.2 to −5.7%/yr with |*t*| between
7.2 and 9.8 on non-overlapping data. All four point estimates agree to within 50 bp/yr;
it is only the precision that is contested, and even the most conservative reading clears
the bar. Block-bootstrap CI on the naive drag (2,000 draws, 21-day blocks): BITO vs IBIT
**[−6.62, −3.84]%/yr**; BITO vs BTC-USD **[−10.45, −0.66]%/yr** (the coin ruler's width is
the timestamp offset, again).

**HAC bandwidth sensitivity** — the residual basis wanders at multi-month scale, so the
default 20-lag window is generous. Widening it:

| lags | full drag *t* | post drag *t* | era-change *t* | matched-window *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 20 | −35.8 | −29.3 | −9.50 | −0.08 |
| 60 | −21.8 | −20.0 | −7.02 | −0.09 |
| 120 | −16.5 | −17.5 | −6.57 | −0.10 |
| 250 | −13.9 | −17.7 | −7.34 | −0.10 |

Every conclusion below survives at 250 lags.

## Implied annualised basis (uses the fee + collateral ASSUMPTIONS)

A fully collateralised long futures wrapper earns `spot − basis + collateral − fee`, so
`basis = cash − fee − drag` and `excess basis = basis − cash = −fee − drag` (the second
does not depend on the cash assumption at all).

| Era | Drag | Cash (BIL) | Implied basis | Excess of cash |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Pre-launch 2021-10-20 → 2024-01-10 | −2.55%/yr | 2.89% | **+4.49%/yr** | +1.60%/yr |
| Post-launch 2024-01-11 → 2026-06-30 | −5.97%/yr | 4.42% | **+9.44%/yr** | +5.02%/yr |

Fee sweep on the post-launch basis: 0.75% → +9.64, 0.95% → +9.44, 1.15% → +9.24%/yr.
The fee shifts the level one-for-one and changes nothing qualitative.

## The era test — did the launch compress the carry?

Broken-trend fit `c_t = a + b·t + g·1{t>t₀} + h·(t−t₀)·1{t>t₀}`; **positive `h` = the drag
shrank = the carry compressed**. The level dummy `g` absorbs any one-day jump.

| Cut | Pre | Post | Change *h* | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Full sample (2021-10 → 2026-06) | −2.56%/yr | −5.97%/yr | **−3.41 pp** | **−9.50** |
| Matched ±12 months around the launch | −7.32%/yr | −7.35%/yr | **−0.03 pp** | **−0.08** |

The two cuts point in opposite directions, and the second is the more comparable one. On
the full sample the carry appears to have *widened* — but only because the pre-launch
window is mostly the **2022 backwardation**, when BITO nearly kept pace with spot. Compare
the twelve months either side of the event and the drag is **identical to within 3 bp/yr**
(*t* = −0.08).

**But "twelve months" is a choice, so here is the whole family** ([`strategy.matched_window_sweep`](../etf_basis/strategy.py)):

| Symmetric window | Pre | Post | Change *h* | HAC *t* | n |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| ±6 months | −7.40%/yr | −9.60%/yr | −2.20 pp | −2.47 | 252 |
| ±9 months | −7.19%/yr | −8.08%/yr | −0.89 pp | −1.31 | 379 |
| **±12 months** | **−7.32%/yr** | **−7.35%/yr** | **−0.03 pp** | **−0.08** | 502 |
| ±18 months | −2.76%/yr | −7.26%/yr | −4.50 pp | −6.43 | 753 |
| ±24 months | −2.23%/yr | −6.68%/yr | −4.45 pp | −12.04 | 1,003 |

**Not one width shows compression.** Every single one is zero or *wrong-signed*, so the
conclusion does not depend on the window — but the ±12-month row quoted as the headline is
the **flattest member of its own family**, i.e. the reading most favourable to "the launch
changed nothing", and it is labelled as such rather than presented as the neutral answer.
The widths disagree for a mundane reason: at ±18 and ±24 months the pre-window starts
swallowing the 2022 backwardation again (pre drops from −7.3 to −2.2%/yr), while at ±6
months the post-window is the Jan-Jul 2024 melt-up when the basis was at its richest. The
one thing no width will produce is the compression the thesis predicted.

**Placebo split sweep.** Re-running the same broken-trend test at 44 arbitrary
month-start dates: median |*t*| = **4.48**, max **10.48**. The launch date's |*t*| = 9.50
ranks only **7 of 44** — 16% of arbitrary dates produce a break at least as "significant".
A slowly wandering basis manufactures large break statistics almost anywhere; the event
date is not special.

## Calendar-year fingerprint — the carry follows the cycle, not the plumbing

| Year | Drag vs BTC-USD | HAC *t* | Drag vs IBIT | Cash | Implied basis |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 2022 | −2.61%/yr | −3.42 | — | 1.43% | +3.09%/yr |
| 2023 | −7.08%/yr | −24.4 | — | 5.01% | +11.14%/yr |
| **2024** (launch year) | −7.41%/yr | −21.6 | −7.18%/yr | 5.20% | +11.66%/yr |
| 2025 | −5.31%/yr | −30.4 | −5.08%/yr | 4.15% | +8.51%/yr |
| 2026 H1 (partial) | −3.13%/yr | −7.80 | −3.07%/yr | 3.49% | +5.67%/yr |

2023 (no spot ETF) and 2024 (spot ETFs live from day 8) are the same number. The basis
tracks the bitcoin cycle — richest through the 2023-24 melt-up, thinnest in the 2022
bear and again in the 2026 drawdown — and the *gradual* compression that does exist
(−7.4 → −3.1 over two and a half years) starts a year late and looks like a cycle, not a
structural break. A rolling-126-day version of the drag against the trailing 126-day
bitcoin return ([`strategy.cycle_regression`](../etf_basis/strategy.py)) correlates
**−0.32**, slope −2.91 %/yr per unit of trailing log return, HAC(250) *t* = **−1.89**:
suggestive, **not certified**. The naive OLS *t* on the same regression is −15.04 — the
windows overlap 126 deep and there are only ~8 independent ones in the sample, so that
number is meaningless and is printed only to show the size of the inflation.

## Tradability — long IBIT / short BITO

Equal-notional pair, reset every 21 sessions using the close of day *t* and live from
*t+1* (**the single execution lag**); the short leg pays borrow every day it is on and
both legs pay one-way cost × NAV on the notional traded at each reset.

**Financing convention (an ASSUMPTION).** The book is dollar-neutral and self-financing:
the short proceeds pay for the long leg, and the rebate earned on those proceeds is
assumed to offset exactly the cash the long leg gives up. The returns below are therefore
already **excess of cash on both legs** — there is no risk-free rate left to subtract, and
none is subtracted. `borrow` is the *incremental* stock-loan fee on top of that wash,
which is why it is swept to 5%: that column is the honest stand-in for a world where the
rebate collapses. Both legs are total return, so the short pays away every BITO
distribution.

| Borrow | Cost | Net | Vol | Sharpe | HAC *t* | Worst DD |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 0% | 0 bps | +5.39%/yr | 1.90% | +2.83 | +7.31 | −0.50% |
| 1% | 5 bps | +4.27%/yr | 1.90% | +2.25 | +5.81 | −0.59% |
| **2%** | **5 bps** | **+3.28%/yr** | 1.90% | **+1.72** | **+4.47** | −0.67% |
| 5% | 5 bps | +0.30%/yr | 1.90% | +0.16 | +0.41 | −1.69% |

Bootstrap Sharpe CI at 2% borrow / 5 bps: **+1.72 [+0.95, +2.48]** (0.0% of resamples
negative). FBTC as the long leg: +3.20%/yr net, Sharpe +1.69, *t* = +4.31.

Inference on the harvest, checked three ways at 2% borrow / 5 bps: HAC *t* = +4.48 (20
lags), +4.17 (60), **+3.74 (250)**; and on **non-overlapping monthly** returns — no HAC at
all — +3.21%/yr with a plain *t* of **+4.35** over 30 months, **28 of 30 positive**. Unlike
the drag measurement, the daily net series is *negatively* autocorrelated (AR(1) −0.34,
the rebalance sawtooth), so here HAC raises the *t* rather than lowering it; the monthly
cross-check confirms it is not an artefact.

Per year at 2% borrow / 5 bps — the harvest is **decaying**:

| Year | Gross | Net | Sharpe | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 2024 | +6.67% | +4.50% | +1.93 | +2.82 |
| 2025 | +5.29% | +3.22% | +2.21 | +3.82 |
| 2026 H1 | +3.06% | +0.99% | +0.56 | +0.82 |

## Synthetic control (machinery proof only — never supports a stamp)

On a planted world (a spot wrapper bleeding a known fee, a futures wrapper bleeding
`fee + basis − collateral`, and closes stamped at a different hour from the reference):

- the ruler recovers the planted 0.25% fee (reads −0.285%/yr);
- with a planted **+7.00 pp** compression at the event the era test reads **+7.31 pp**
  (*t* = +33.2) — the detector fires;
- with **no** compression but the *same large drag* in both halves it reads **+0.31 pp**
  (*t* = +1.43); across eight seeds the change is centred at **+0.09 pp** (sd 0.22) and
  never reaches 2 pp (0/8). The detector does not invent a break out of a big level.

## Verdict

- **Signal — Mixed.** Two findings, opposite colours. (i) The futures wrapper's carry is
  **unambiguously still there** after the spot ETFs: **−5.72%/yr against IBIT on matched
  closes**, certified on the estimator that assumes least — 29 non-overlapping monthly
  gaps, plain *t* = **−9.83**, with the endpoint estimator agreeing at −7.24. The trend
  slope's *t* = −30.7 is reported but discounted (that residual is near a unit root, DF
  *t* = −3.0). Against the coin the drag is −5.97%/yr (trend *t* = −29.3, −17.7 at 250
  lags) but only −2.17 on the blunt monthly ruler — the timestamp offset again. An implied
  front basis
  of **+9.4%/yr**, +5.0%/yr above cash — Real-grade, on a ruler calibrated to read a 25 bp
  fee exactly. (ii) The claim actually
  under test — that the January-2024 launch **compressed** that basis — is **rejected**:
  matched twelve-month windows either side read −7.32 vs −7.35%/yr (change −0.03 pp,
  *t* = −0.08), and the full-sample "significant" break (*t* = −9.50) has the *wrong sign*
  and ranks a mediocre 7/44 against placebo split dates. What compression exists arrives
  in 2025-26 and tracks the bitcoin cycle. No survivorship: three live, continuously
  listed instruments, no cross-section, no selection — though BITO is the *surviving*
  futures wrapper, so if anything the class-wide toll is understated.
- **Tradability — Fragile.** Long IBIT / short BITO nets **+3.28%/yr at 2% borrow and
  5 bps**, excess of cash on both legs (Sharpe 1.72, HAC *t* = +4.47 and +3.74 at 250
  lags, non-overlapping monthly *t* = +4.35 with 28/30 months positive, bootstrap CI
  [+0.95, +2.48], worst drawdown
  0.67%) — genuinely bankable *if* you can borrow BITO cheaply, and dead at 5% borrow
  (+0.30%/yr, *t* = +0.41). The spread is also shrinking year by year (net +4.50% →
  +3.22% → +0.99%), it is capacity-bounded by BITO's borrow pool, and the risk-free
  version of the trade — simply own the spot wrapper instead — is cost avoidance, not
  alpha.
